title: Handle ordering in plain highlighter for multiple inputs

timeline.message: Handle ordering in plain highlighter for multiple inputs
timeline.author: Alan Woodward

timeline.body:
The ordering logic in the plain highlighter only worked for single-valued
inputs.  If you had multiple inputs, then order-by-score would only do this
ordering for fragments within each input, and order-by-position would 
interleave fragments from the different inputs.  This commit fixes both
issues.

Fixes #87210

timeline.body: Just out of curiosity, did you consider making the list sorted from the start or would this have major drawbacks? I didn't clearly check whether sorting is always done here, maybe not and thats the reason why we don't need a sorted list from the start...

reply.body: The highlighter outputs fragments sorted by score, so if we only have a single input and we want score order then there's no need to do anything.  Otherwise we need to re-sort

timeline.body: Also just curious about the switch from Lucene CollectionUtil to plain list sort here, any pros / cons about the former?

reply.body: Just that it means we get to use built-in collections; it's possible that lucene's introSort is slightly more efficient, but we're talking tiny lists and small sets of results so I thought clarity was more important.

timeline.body: Left to questions for my own education, otherwise LGTM
